Shipped engines plus the schema generated from DATABASE.md.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .db import Database, PersistenceError, UnknownOperation\nfrom .schema import SCHEMA, open_database\n\n__all__ = [\"Database\", \"PersistenceError\", \"SCHEMA\", \"UnknownOperation\", \"open_database\"]\n\"\"\"Generated fixtures over the configured, already provisioned application store.\"\"\"\n\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .schema import open_database\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef committed_session():\n    \"\"\"Use normal autocommit for project tests; under the acceptance harness, its transaction.\"\"\"\n    configured = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\") or os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\") or \"data/app.db\"\n    if not configured.startswith((\"postgres://\", \"postgresql://\")):\n        if not Path(configured.split(\"://\", 1)[-1]).is_file():\n            raise RuntimeError(\"persistence store missing; rebuild the DATABASE step\")\n    database = open_database(configured)\n    try:\n        yield database\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef db_session():\n    \"\"\"Share this connection with the feature; always roll back, never provision schema.\n\n    Under the acceptance harness the rollback is the harness's, at the end of the criterion, so\n    a request made after this block still sees the setup.\n    \"\"\"\n    with committed_session() as database:\n        with database.rollback_session():\n            yield database\n----\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``name`` is the method callers use and ``verb`` is its Kind, how it runs; a name that is a\n    verb runs as that verb. ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies. ``match`` is the\n    equality predicate of a ``get``, ``update``, ``upsert``, or ``delete``, every field of it\n    required; a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n----\n\"\"\"Database location precedence: DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then the default.\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom ledger_core.config import database_path\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef clean_environment(monkeypatch):\n    \"\"\"Start every test with neither variable set so the inherited store cannot leak in.\"\"\"\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", raising=False)\n    monkeypatch.delenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", raising=False)\n\n\ndef test_default_path_when_no_variable_is_set():\n    assert database_path() == \"data/app.db\"\n\n\ndef test_database_url_is_used_alone(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"plain.db\")\n    assert database_path() == \"plain.db\"\n\n\ndef test_database_url_sqlite_prefix_is_removed(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"sqlite://primary.db\")\n    assert database_path() == \"primary.db\"\n\n\ndef test_database_url_wins_over_database_path(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"sqlite://primary.db\")\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"fallback.db\")\n    assert database_path() == \"primary.db\"\n\n\ndef test_empty_database_url_falls_through_to_database_path(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"\")\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"fallback.db\")\n    assert database_path() == \"fallback.db\"\n\n\ndef test_database_path_alone_is_used(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"fallback.db\")\n    assert database_path() == \"fallback.db\"\n\n\ndef test_empty_database_path_falls_through_to_default(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"\")\n    assert database_path() == \"data/app.db\"\n\n\ndef test_empty_url_and_path_fall_through_to_default(monkeypatch):\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"\")\n    monkeypatch.setenv(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"\")\n    assert database_path() == \"data/app.db\"\n\n\"\"\"Domain error classes and their exit codes.\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom ledger_core.errors import LedgerError, NotFound, Operational, Rejected\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    (\"cls\", \"code\"),\n    [(Rejected, 3), (NotFound, 4), (Operational, 1)],\n)\ndef test_error_class_carries_exit_code(cls, code):\n    assert cls(\"probe\").exit_code == code\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"cls\", [Rejected, NotFound, Operational])\ndef test_error_class_derives_from_ledger_error(cls):\n    assert issubclass(cls, LedgerError)\n\n\ndef test_error_keeps_its_message():\n    assert str(Rejected(\"duplicate account\")) == \"duplicate account\"\n\"\"\"Project foundation: files, importable packages, and the static rules on domain code.\"\"\"\n\nimport ast\nimport importlib\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nDOMAIN_ROOT = ROOT / \"ledger_core\"\nBANNED_DRIVERS = {\"sqlite3\", \"psycopg\", \"psycopg2\"}\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"name\", [\"pyproject.toml\", \"uv.lock\", \"conftest.py\", \"bin/test.sh\"])\ndef test_project_file_exists(name):\n    assert (ROOT / name).is_file()\n\n\ndef test_test_launcher_runs_pytest():\n    assert \"pytest\" in (ROOT / \"bin\" / \"test.sh\").read_text()\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"module\", [\"ledger_core\", \"ledger_core.config\", \"ledger_core.errors\"])\ndef test_foundation_module_imports(module):\n    assert importlib.import_module(module) is not None\n\n\ndef _domain_files():\n    return sorted(DOMAIN_ROOT.rglob(\"*.py\"))\n\n\ndef test_domain_files_are_scanned():\n    assert len(_domain_files()) >= 1\n\n\ndef _imported_top_level_names(tree):\n    for node in ast.walk(tree):\n        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):\n            for alias in node.names:\n                yield alias.name.split(\".\")[0]\n        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):\n            yield (node.module or \"\").split(\".\")[0]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", _domain_files(), ids=lambda p: str(p.relative_to(ROOT)))\ndef test_domain_module_imports_no_database_driver(path):\n    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())\n    assert not (BANNED_DRIVERS & set(_imported_top_level_names(tree)))\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", _domain_files(), ids=lambda p: str(p.relative_to(ROOT)))\ndef test_domain_module_has_no_float_call_or_literal(path):\n    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())\n    float_calls = [\n        node\n        for node in ast.walk(tree)\n        if isinstance(node, ast.Call)\n        and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name)\n        and node.func.id == \"float\"\n    ]\n    float_literals = [\n        node\n        for node in ast.walk(tree)\n        if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, float)\n    ]\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgStkkyjoVKPR9HgJ1JfN","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01B5iM7k8fN6JowtBwG3g2By","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/LayersTesting/runs/20261027.135355/build/LayersTesting/cli/__init__.py","content":"\"\"\"Command-line entry point for the ledger.\n\n``main`` resolves the command words, checks the argument count, opens the database, calls the\nhandler, and turns the result into CSV on stdout or one diagnostic line on stderr. It returns the\nexit code and never calls ``sys.exit``; the ``ledger`` launcher is the only caller that does.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli import registry\nfrom ledger_core.config import database_path\nfrom ledger_core.errors import LedgerError\nfrom persistence import open_database\n\nEXIT_OK = 0\nEXIT_OPERATIONAL = 1\nEXIT_USAGE = 2\n\n\ndef _usage_error(message: str) -> int:\n    print(f\"usage: {message}\", file=sys.stderr)\n    return EXIT_USAGE\n\n\ndef _match(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], registry.Command] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the longest command-word prefix of ``argv`` that is registered, with its command.\"\"\"\n    for length in range(len(argv), 0, -1):\n        words = tuple(argv[:length])\n        if words in registry.COMMANDS:\n            return words, registry.COMMANDS[words]\n    return None\n\n\ndef _format(rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render rows as unquoted CSV with ``\\\\n`` line endings.\"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(\",\".join(str(value) for value in row) + \"\\n\" for row in rows)\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)\n    registry.load()\n\n    matched = _match(argv)\n    if matched is None:\n        return _usage_error(f\"unknown command {' '.join(argv)!r}\" if argv else \"no command given\")\n    words, command = matched\n\n    args = argv[len(words):]\n    if len(args) < command.min_args or (command.max_args is not None and len(args) > command.max_args):\n        return _usage_error(f\"wrong number of arguments for {' '.join(words)!r}\")\n\n    try:\n        database = open_database(database_path())\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"error: cannot open database: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return EXIT_OPERATIONAL\n\n    try:\n        rows = command.handler(database, args)\n    except LedgerError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return EXIT_OPERATIONAL\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n    sys.stdout.write(_format(rows))\n    return EXIT_OK\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6461,"cache_read_input_tokens":42859,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6461},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d08aac72-8272-43d6-89b6-8c872a247c21","uuid":"093dfb9d-ff3a-4792-b74c-00cce1bc04bd","timestamp":"2026-10-27T14:23:33.890Z","request_id":"req_011CgStkkeepw5FXiP4Gjo8W","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_01B5iM7k8fN6JowtBwG3g2By":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/LayersTesting/runs/20261027.135355/build/LayersTesting/cli/__init__.py","content":"\"\"\"Command-line stderr. It returns the\nexit code and never calls ``sys.exit``; the ``ledger`` launcher is the only caller that does.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli import registry\nfrom ledger_core.config import database_path\nfrom ledger_core.errors import LedgerError\nfrom persistence import open_database\n\nEXIT_OK = 0\nEXIT_OPERATIONAL = 1\nEXIT_USAGE = 2\n\n\ndef _usage_error(message: str) -> int:\n    print(f\"usage: {message}\", file=sys.stderr)\n    return EXIT_USAGE\n\n\ndef _match(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], registry.Command] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the longest command-word prefix of ``argv`` that is registered, with its command.\"\"\"\n    for length in range(len(argv), 0, -1):\n        words = tuple(argv[:length])\n        if words in registry.COMMANDS:\n            return words, registry.COMMANDS[words]\n    return None\n\n\ndef _format(rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render rows as unquoted CSV with ``\\\\n`` line endings.\"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(\",\".join(str(value) for value in row) + \"\\n\" for row in rows)\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)\n    registry.load()\n\n    matched = _match(argv)\n    if matched is None:\n        return _usage_error(f\"unknown command {' '.join(argv)!r}\" if argv else \"no command given\")\n    words, command = matched\n\n    args = argv[len(words):]\n    if len(args) < command.min_args or (command.max_args is not None and len(args) > command.max_args):\n        return _usage_error(f\"wrong number of arguments for {' '.join(words)!r}\")\n\n    try:\n        database = open_database(database_path())\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"error: cannot open database: {exc}\",  return exc.exit_code\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return EXIT_OPERATIONAL\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n    sys.stdout.write(_format(rows))\n    return EXIT_OK\n"}}}

It returns the\nexit code and never calls ``sys.exit``; the ``ledger`` launcher is the only caller that does.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom cli import registry\nfrom ledger_core.config import database_path\nfrom ledger_core.errors import LedgerError, Operational\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nEXIT_OK = 0\nEXIT_OPERATIONAL = 1\nEXIT_USAGE = 2\nPOSTGRES_PREFIXES = (\"postgres://\", \"postgresql://\")\n\n\ndef _usage_error(message: str) -> int:\n    print(f\"usage: {message}\", file=sys.stderr)\n    return EXIT_USAGE\n\n\ndef _open_store(location: str) -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the declared store. A SQLite file whose directory is absent is refused, not created.\n\n    The shipped SQLite driver creates a missing parent directory on connect, which would turn a\n    mistyped location into a new, empty store. The ledger's store is provisioned in advance.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not location.startswith(POSTGRES_PREFIXES):\n        parent = Path(location).parent\n        if not parent.is_dir():\n            raise Operational(f\"database directory does not exist: {parent}\")\n    return open_database(location)\n\n\ndef _match(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], registry.Command] | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the longest command-word prefix of ``argv`` that is registered, with its command.\"\"\"\n    for length in range(len(argv), 0, -1):\n        words = tuple(argv[:length])\n        if words in registry.COMMANDS:\n            return words, registry.COMMANDS[words]\n    return None\n\n\ndef _format(rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render rows as unquoted CSV with ``\\\\n`` line endings.\"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(\",\".join(str(value) for value in row) + \"\\n\" for row in rows)\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)\n    registry.load()\n\n    matched = _match(argv)\n    if matched is None:\n        return _usage_error(f\"unknown command {' '.join(argv)!r}\" if argv else \"no command given\")\n    words, command = matched\n\n    args = argv[len(words):]\n    if len(args) < command.min_args or (command.max_args is not None and len(args) > command.max_args):\n        return _usage_error(f\"wrong number of arguments for {' '.join(words)!r}\")\n\n    try:\n        database = open_database(database_path())\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"error: cannot open database: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return EXIT_OPERATIONAL\n\n    try:\n        rows = command.handler(database, args)\n    except LedgerError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return exc.exit_code\n    except Exception as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return EXIT_OPERATIONAL\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n    sys.stdout.write(_format(rows))\n    return EXIT_OK\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":65,"oldLines":7,"newStart":65,"newLines":7,"lines":["         return _usage_error(f\"wrong number of arguments for {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgSttLtP2nw4Xh6WptBJs","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Everything is in place. The launcher is executable on disk, but `core.fileMode` is `false` in this repo, so git may record it as `100644` when committed. I'll flag that rather than change git config.\n\n**Result summary before the final block:** the `ledger` story is built and the full suite passes (53 tests, `bin/test.sh` exit 0). I did not commit, as instructed.\n\n<reusable-compact filename=\"DATABASE.md\">\nDatabase: LayersTesting (version 20261027 V1). Build order 1. Provides persistence.accounts, persistence.categories, persistence.transactions.\n\nAccess: `open_database(dsn)` returns `Database`; `db.<table>.<op>(...)`. Money: integer cents everywhere. No aggregate operations; callers compute counts, sums, next txn_id from list results.\n\nOperations (input -> output; * = match key):\n- accounts.create(account, name) -> (account, name)\n- accounts.get(account*) -> (account, name) | None\n- accounts.update(account*, name) -> (account, name)\n- accounts.delete(account*) -> (account)\n- accounts.list() -> [(account, name)] order account asc\n- accounts.clear(min_account) -> count; removes account >= min_account; \"\" removes all\n- categories.create(category, description) -> (category, description)\n- categories.get(category*) -> (category, description) | None\n- categories.update(category*, description) -> (category, description)\n- categories.delete(category*) -> (category)\n- categories.list() -> [(category, description)] order category asc\n- categories.clear(min_category) -> count; \"\" removes all\n- transactions.create(txn_id, date, account, category, amount, memo) -> (txn_id, date, account, category, amount, memo)\n- transactions.get(txn_id*) -> row | None\n- transactions.update(txn_id*, amount) -> row\n- transactions.delete(txn_id*) -> (txn_id)\n- transactions.list(account?, category?, start_date?, end_date?) -> [row] filters account, category, date>=start_date, date<=end_date; order txn_id asc\n- transactions.clear(min_txn_id) -> count; 0 removes all\n\nSchema:\n- accounts(account TEXT PK, 1-12 chars A-Z0-9; name TEXT NOT NULL, 1-40 chars)\n- categories(category TEXT PK, 1-12 chars A-Z0-9; description TEXT NOT NULL, 1-40 chars)\n- transactions(txn_id INTEGER PK; date TEXT YYYY-MM-DD; account FK accounts; category FK categories; amount INTEGER cents signed, never zero; memo TEXT 0-60 chars default ''); INDEX(account, date)\n\nConfig: DATABASE_URL (SQLite path, optional sqlite:// prefix, wins), DATABASE_PATH (fallback), default data/app.db.\n\nGuardrails: only the persistence package opens a driver;
